subject: Geography
description: Covers Great Circle, IDL, IST calculation.

questions.stem: Which of the following imaginary lines is also known as the 'Great Circle' because it divides the Earth into two equal hemispheres?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: The Equator (0 degrees latitude) is the only line of latitude that is a 'Great Circle'. A great circle is any circle drawn on a globe that shares the exact same center as the globe itself, dividing it into two mathematically equal halves (the Northern and Southern Hemispheres). 
DECOY BUSTING: All lines of longitude (meridians) are great circles, but the Equator is the ONLY line of latitude that is one. The Tropics are 'Small Circles' because they don't share the Earth's center. The Prime Meridian is only half of a great circle (it needs the 180th meridian on the other side to complete it).
EXAM INSIGHT: Aircraft and ships always try to travel along 'Great Circle Routes' because they represent the absolute shortest distance between two points on the spherical surface of the Earth.

questions.stem: The International Date Line (IDL), where the date officially changes by one day as you cross it, roughly follows which line of longitude?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: The International Date Line roughly follows the 180-degree meridian of longitude, sitting in the middle of the Pacific Ocean, exactly opposite the Prime Meridian. If you cross the IDL traveling West (towards Asia), you add a day. If you cross it traveling East (towards America), you subtract a day.
DECOY BUSTING: The Prime Meridian (0 degrees) passes through Greenwich, London, and is the baseline for global Time (GMT/UTC), but it does not dictate the Date change.
EXAM INSIGHT: The IDL is not a perfectly straight line. It intentionally zigzags to avoid splitting single countries or island groups (like Kiribati and the Aleutian Islands) into two different calendar days, which would cause administrative chaos.

questions.stem: When it is 12:00 Noon in London (Greenwich Mean Time - GMT), what is the standard time in India (Indian Standard Time - IST)?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Indian Standard Time (IST) is calculated based on the 82.5° East longitude, which passes through Mirzapur (near Prayagraj/Allahabad) in Uttar Pradesh. Because the Earth rotates 15 degrees every hour, an 82.5-degree shift eastward equates to exactly 5.5 hours. Since India is East of Greenwich, we are AHEAD of their time. Therefore, 12:00 Noon + 5.5 hours = 5:30 PM.
DECOY BUSTING: 5:30 AM would be the time if India was West of Greenwich (like parts of the USA).
EXAM INSIGHT: Despite its massive width spanning nearly 30 degrees of longitude (which translates to a 2-hour actual time difference between Gujarat and Arunachal Pradesh), India officially observes only ONE single time zone to avoid railway and administrative confusion.
